notes.text: The working sheet is headed underlined Proposition, with vertical marginal strokes. It defines the two principal sets C_geqx and C_leqx, then writes that they are tot with a raised t/l ordonnés. The abbreviation tt and the live les / cancelled group / live ens. sequence are preserved. Pencil archive number 39 is recorded only as a comment; no authorial date was observed.

The attempted proof has raised le and pour, an uncertainly cancelled le/la article, an older crossed notons/noter above premier and an uncertain detached point before it. Cel/cela and aussi/ceci are retained from the compressed bodies. A following display begins capital Si. The ink and revision layers govern these readings.

The sketch has lower x, upper-left z, upper-right y, an additional unlabelled upper-centre dot, four arrowheads and three detached strokes. The adjacent bracket says non congrus mod sigma, à cause de 28 a),. The last comma belongs inside the closing bracket.

The proof rewrites x as y and y as z. The old letters and their overwritten state remain marked. Incomparables carries no independent underline under in. The punctuation immediately after it has a high point and a low comma stroke.

Both lower comparison signs display a diagonal branch and two lower strokes. The written less-than-or-equal forms are preserved independently of the argument. The word before peut remains peu/pas/ne. The separate point after on is preserved. The old ne peut avoir group is cancelled and the whole aurait donc is raised.
The last line ends after sigma z < with one isolated falling-right stroke. Its function remains open. Neither the mathematical calculation nor the witnesses supply an unwritten operand.

SA01-K81-02 quotes the opening proposition and reports a tripod counterexample. The local statement crop confirms both written principal sets and the tot abbreviation. This run checks a concrete six-element structure below. The supplied sweep mentions c81checks.py and 18,247 labelled trees; that script is absent from the package, and that larger computation was not reproduced.

The finite certificate uses the graph with vertices {0,1,2,3} and edges 01,02,03. Its six oriented cuts are named iL and iR for i=1,2,3; the explicit map sends iL to {i} and iR to the complement of {i}. The inverse map is listed for every one of these six distinct subsets. Both inverse identities are checked. Sigma swaps each pair. Strict order is proper inclusion, and comparability includes equality. Graph traversal after each deleted edge independently computes the same six displayed subsets.

For these six entries, the relation displayed in (26), distinct edge indices together with A intersect sigma(B) empty, agrees with proper inclusion on all 36 ordered pairs. The certificate checks irreflexivity on 6 entries, asymmetry on 36 pairs, transitivity on 216 triples, the fixed-point-free involution on all 6 entries and the written clause (28) comparisons on all 36 pairs.

The concrete upper-set failure is x={1}, y={0,1,3}, z={0,1,2}. Both proper inclusions from x hold. The two differences y minus z={3} and z minus y={2} witness the incomparability of y,z. The lower set at {0,2,3} contains the incomparable singletons {2},{3}. Thus the two total-order assertions fail in this explicit structure. All twelve intervals in this same structure are enumerated and are chains; no general replacement theorem is stated.

The computed sigma(y)={2} lies properly in z, while sigma(z)={3} lies properly in y and does not lie in x. These particular values are recorded only in the mathematical note and certificate. The unfinished final operand in the transcription is preserved exactly as seen.

Three C doubts are resolved and eleven retained; fifteen uncertainty loci remain in the text. R1’s H difference for the expanded tot is declined because H explicitly supplies the abbreviation mapping.
